newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Upbeat Australian stocks end higher as Dow bounces.
newsitem.headline: Upbeat Australian stocks end higher as Dow bounces.

text.p: SPI 2363 +7 US 30yr cl 7.17 steady
10yrbond futs 92.030 +0.085 Gold NY 346.25 Lon fix 346.75
*Stocks end with respectable gains after Wall St bounces back, volumes only moderate. Volume 247.29 million, value A$669.24 million, 1,014 stocks traded, 287 steady, 469 up, 258 down.
Australian shares chalked up respectable gains on Tuesday in response to a rebound on Wall Street after Friday's inflation fear-inspired selloff.
However, volumes remained subdued and brokers said the scarcity of investor interest ahead of further U.S. inflation figures had perhaps exaggerated some of the gains made.
At 4.25 p.m. (0625 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was up 15.6 points at 2,381.7.
The June share price index was up seven points at 2,363 and at an 18.7 point discount to the underlying index.
"Our market is not all that active," said dealer Jamie Spiteri of Shaw Stockbroking, noting that the lack of aggressive interest on either side had helped the day's upside bias.
"It is probably a little bit tight actually, so when some buying does come into the market, these prices tend to move up further than what some people anticipate."
The cautious display, amid a generally upbeat tone, was linked to further inflation figures, namely the U.S. consumer price index, due later on Tuesday.
"As you would expect, traders remain cautious," Spiteri said.
Oil stocks featured on the day, the energy index jumping 2.4 percent compared to a gain in the benchmark All Ordinaries index of 0.7 percent.
Brokers said a combination of firmer oil prices and an optimistic exploration outlook had fuelled much of the group's positive sentiment.

Sector leader Woodside Petroleum, up 26 cents to A$9.60 accounted for much of the gains but Novus Petroleum, closing up 20 cents at A$3.65 after it announced the US$26.5 million purchase of further equity in the Bukha gas condensate field in Oman, also impressed.

Elsewhere in the resources, gold miner Plutonic Resources rocketed nearly 10 percent to an intraday high of A$5.05 before easing to close 5.5 percent higher at A$4.85 after it announced a doubling of the gold resource at its Centenary deposit in Western Australia.
In the industrials, Rupert Murdoch's media behemoth News Corporation ended 11 cents higher at A$5.83.

However, traders said the rise was due to general market movements rather than the appointment of his son Lachlan Murdoch as head of Australian operations. Lachlan is to replace his father's long-time lieutenant, Ken Cowley.
In the smaller industrials, contract labour suplier Skilled Engineering continued to feel the fallout from a review of the cable rollout of telecoms group, Optus Comunications.
Skilled Engineering shares closed over 10 percent lower at A$2.39.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about nine to five, while about 28 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Futures trade was active as sellers quickly covered positions although options trade was average.
Total options traded was 34,504.
Turnover in June SPI contracts totalled 9,564.

In other local markets, Australian bonds yields were sharply lower in anticipation that key local data over the next couple of weeks will be friendly, and shaking off the anxiety over Federal Reserve policy which continues to dog the U.S.
By 5.10 p.m. (0710 GMT), 10 year T-bonds were yielding 7.93 percent compared to Monday's 8.02 percent levels.

The Australian dollar succumbed to stronger local bond with heavy offshore selling and ended well down on Monday's late levels. By 5.10 p.m. (0710 GMT), the local dollar had caved to US$0.7756/61, having sunk to US$0.7774/79 at the opening from US$0.7815/20 late Monday and a US$0.7895 peak last Friday.
